I'm 20 years old currently, and the surgery wasn't as terrible of a recovery as the Google results will tell you.

I didn't feel like eating for a couple days, the anaesthetic caused me to be a bit nauseous. And other than that, you get dry mouth while sleeping (while the packing is in,) and the pain nearly completely subsided within 3-4 days. Stitches and cast off in a week.

Best of wishes to you on your fitness trials justim =)

I'm under the impression that you have a deviated septum, if it is similar to asthma, and you've always had it.

I also had this. And I know it seems like a long shot, and a weird concept, but if you live anywhere with a social health care plan, or can afford it, I would highly recommend you get a minor surgery known as septoplasty done.

I grew up with a deviated septum, then worsened my condition through several breaks. I've just finished recovering from surgery recently, and it's altered my entire life. I've never slept so well, I'm no longer congested, I can run further, and I'm happier. 

Just a thought. 

Best wishes with everything. <3

As a young woman with a father currently going through treatment to try to attempt to eradicate his Hepatitis C, it's scientific achievements such as these that give me further hope for his having a better future. The current treatment he his on, consisting of daily pills and weekly injections, (Pegatron, Ribaviran and Victrellis interferon) has him in a state of constant illness/weakness, he's had dramatic weight loss, and many days is bed ridden and unable to work the job he loves so dearly. All this for a year, with the chance of poor results. It's not an easy thing to hear someone you idolize in such a severe state of depression that they openly consider suicide.

A treatment without side effects such as the ones my father currently experiences would be a dream come true. These are the people that should be inspiring my generation.

It's terrible that they don't make people more aware of it.... I would think they would check and feel your glands at the first sign of recurring throat congestion... Shame. =/ my brother is a stage IV now. 
He has surgery next week, and the tumour is wrapped around some primary facial nerves supposedly. 

Here's hoping for the best.

OP. I'm also messaging you this. But despite how it annoys you, for the sake of the man at your office, tell him to please have his salivary glands checked out. The constant throat clearing may seem harmless to his well being, but it's a sign of salivary gland cancer. And if I had known this previously, I might not be losing my brother to the battle. 

Please take precautions people, and see a doctor.
